content: 1. Patients who have developed physical dependence on fentanyl may experience increased plasma concentrations of fentanyl after discontinuing a CYP3A4 inducer. This increase can prolong or intensify both therapeutic and adverse effects of fentanyl. 2. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels and effects of transdermal fentanyl by enhancing its metabolism through hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 3. Co-administration of fentanyl with CYP3A4 inducers can lead to reduced fentanyl plasma concentrations, diminished efficacy, or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. Discontinuation of the inducer may result in increased fentanyl levels, necessitating close monitoring. 4. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of transmucosal fentanyl by accelerating its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of finasteride by affecting its metabolism through hepatic CYP3A4 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of flibanserin by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce systemic exposure to flibanserin. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored. 7. Rifampin reduces fluconazole levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 8. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of fludrocortisone by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of flurazepam by accelerating its metabolism through CYP3A4 enzymes. Therapy adjustments and monitoring are recommended. 10. Rifampin increases the toxicity of fluvastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are required. 11. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of fosphenytoin by enhancing its metabolism via hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Fostamatinib increases the levels and effects of rifampin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Concomitant use may elevate concentrations of P-gp substrates, necessitating monitoring for toxicities and potential dosage reductions. 13. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of gefitinib by accelerating its metabolism through CYP3A4 enzymes. If co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer, the gefitinib dose may need to be increased to 500 mg daily, with a return to 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the inducer. 14. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of gentamicin by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Rifampin reduces the levels of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by increasing their metabolism through hepatic enzymes, including CYP2C9/10. Strong CYP2C9 inducers may further accelerate glyburide metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 16. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of guanfacine by accelerating its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce guanfacine plasma concentrations and elimination half-life. For ADHD patients, doubling the guanfacine dose may be considered. 17. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of haloperidol by enhancing its metabolism through CYP3A4 enzymes. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of hydrocodone by accelerating its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with hydrocodone may increase plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Therapy adjustments and monitoring are essential. 19. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of hydrocortisone by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Rifampin increases the effects of ifosfamide by accelerating its metabolism through CYP2B6 enzymes. Co-administration with CYP2B6 inducers may increase the formation of active alkylating metabolites and neurotoxic/nephrotoxic metabolites like chloroacetaldehyde. Close monitoring for toxicities and dose adjustments are necessary. 21. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of imatinib by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of imipramine by accelerating its metabolism through CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of indinavir by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 24. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of iptacopan by increasing its metabolism via CYP2C8 enzymes. CYP2C8 inducers may reduce iptacopan efficacy. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by enhancing their efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of isradipine by accelerating its metabolism through CYP3A4 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 27. Istradefylline increases the levels and effects of rifampin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Clinical trials have shown increased peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates. Dose reductions of sensitive P-gp substrates should be considered. 28. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of itraconazole by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Ivacaftor increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 30. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of ivermectin by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 31. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of ketamine by accelerating its metabolism through CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of ketoconazole by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 33. Rifampin decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing its metabolism and hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of lapatinib by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Lemborexant decreases rifampin levels by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitoring for adequate clinical response and potential dose adjustments of CYP2B6 substrates is recommended. 36. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of lesinurad by accelerating its metabolism via CYP2C9/10 enzymes. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 37. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of levamlodipine by enhancing its metabolism through CYP3A4 enzymes. Therapy adjustments and monitoring are recommended. 38. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of levonorgestrel (both intrauterine and oral forms) by accelerating its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative or backup contraception should be used during and for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. 39. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of lidocaine by accelerating its metabolism via CYP1A2 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 40. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of linagliptin by enhancing its metabolism via CYP3A4 enzymes and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended when linagliptin is co-administered with a P-gp inducer. 41. Rifampin decreases lofepramine levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Lomitapide increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Dose reductions should be considered when used concomitantly. 43. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of loperamide by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 44. Rifampin decreases the levels and effects of losartan by accelerating its metabolism via CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 enzymes. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 45. Rifampin reduces the levels and effects of lovastatin by enhancing its efflux via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary.
